# Deprecations
Copy Page
This page lists all API deprecations, along with recommended replacements.
## Overview
As we launch safer and more capable models, we regularly retire older models. Software relying on OpenAI models may need occasional updates to keep working. Impacted customers will always be notified by email and in our documentation.
Each model has one of three lifecycle states.
- Active. You can use the model through the API. OpenAI hasn't announced its retirement.
- Deprecated. OpenAI has announced the model's retirement. You can still use it until its shutdown date.
- Shutdown. The model no longer accepts requests through the standard API.
For deprecation notice periods and help migrating to a replacement model, see the deprecation policy and migration guidance below.
See feature and endpoint deprecations for other upcoming API shutdowns.

## Model deprecation notice periods
We provide advance notice before retiring models so customers have time to plan and migrate. When we announce a model deprecation, we notify customers who are actively using the model by email and document the deprecation on this page.
Unless safety or compliance concerns require a faster timeline, we provide the following minimum notice periods before model retirement:
- Generally available models: At least 6 months.
- Specialized variants of generally available models and image generation models: At least 3 months. Examples include chat variants such as gpt-5.1-chat-latest , Codex variants such as gpt-5.3-codex , and deep research variants such as o3-deep-research .
- Preview models: Preview models, identified by preview in the model name, may be retired with much shorter notice, such as 2 weeks. Examples include computer-use-preview and gpt-4o-audio-preview . We don't recommend using preview models for business-critical production workloads unless you can migrate on short notice.
These notice periods give customers time to evaluate recommended replacement models, test application behavior, and complete migrations before a model is no longer available. In some cases, developers may be able to provision dedicated capacity for continued access after a model's shutdown date. To explore this option, contact our sales team .
## Best practices
- Check the documentation regularly for model deprecation updates.
- To monitor model shutdowns programmatically , call the List models endpoint ( GET /v1/models ) and check each model's optional shutdown_date field. The field is also available from the Retrieve a model endpoint .
## Migration guidance
- In Codex, invoke the OpenAI Docs skill with $openai-docs and ask it to migrate your project to the recommended replacement.
- See the GPT-6 migration guide .
- Run representative requests against both models. Compare outputs, latency, and cost before switching production traffic to the replacement.
## Update to OpenAI's self-serve fine-tuning
We previously announced January 6, 2027, as the cutoff for creating new self-serve fine-tuning jobs. We're moving that cutoff up to December 15, 2026 .
You can continue to run inference on each existing fine-tuned model until OpenAI retires its underlying base model.
Date | Update
May 7, 2026 | Organizations that have never run a fine-tuning job can no longer create one.
July 2, 2026 | Organizations that haven't run inference on a fine-tuned model in the past 60 days can no longer create training jobs.
Dec 15, 2026 | Starting on this date, no organization can create new self-serve fine-tuning jobs.

### Historical notes
- Fine-tuned versions of the legacy GPT models shut down in October 2026 followed the same shutdown schedule as their underlying base models.
- The codex-mini-latest shutdown also ended support for the legacy local shell tool. For new integrations, use the shell tool .
- The Assistants API notice followed the release of the Responses API in March 2025 . We first announced plans to retire the Assistants API v1 beta when we released v2 in April 2024 .
- The October 2024 shutdown for fine-tuning training on babbage-002 and davinci-002 applied to creating new fine-tuned models. Existing fine-tuned models were unaffected by that change.
- The June 6, 2024 notice reconfirmed the retirement of gpt-4-32k-0314 . Starting June 17, 2024, access to the GPT-4-32K and Vision Preview models and the GPT-3.5 Turbo snapshots announced in November 2023 was limited to existing users. Existing fine-tuned models from those GPT-3.5 Turbo snapshots were unaffected by that shutdown.
- The legacy fine-tunes endpoint shutdown also removed access to models trained with that endpoint. Developers had to train new models through the updated fine-tuning API .
- The July 2023 announcement covered older GPT-3 and GPT-3.5 models served through the completions endpoint and first-generation text embedding models. See the pricing page for current model pricing.
- The June 2023 announcement gave an earliest retirement date of June 13, 2024 for the original chat models. Starting January 10, 2024, access was limited to existing users. See the March 2026 shutdown notice for the final shutdown date of gpt-4-0314 .
